J01.job: Turn a plain-English request into the right action
notes: One request per command carrying 10 questions; code runs the call only if min confidence >= 0.7.

J02.job: Pick the right tool for an AI agent, or none
notes: 20 skills. Request 1 ranks all skills and asks 3 gate questions; request 2 re-checks the top 3. Gate 0.3, fits 0.3 (cookbook values).

J03.job: Screen what goes into and out of an AI assistant
notes: Policy (fixed before running): block if a blocker >= 0.7; otherwise any hazard >= 0.35 (including destructive >= 0.7) goes to review, upgraded to block when severity >= 2.0.

J04.job: Check that a citation really supports the claim
notes: Code checks the quote exists (exact, or a sentence at least 85% similar) before any model call; one Choice per surviving citation; auto-accept at confidence 0.8.

J05.job: Decide which search results an AI is allowed to read
notes: Four Nouls per query-passage pair; cookbook thresholds applied first-match-wins (injection .70, contradicts .70, relevant .45, evidence .55).

J16.job: Decide whether two records are the same thing
notes: One Score (3 levels) plus three field Nouls per pair; code rounds the score: >= 1.5 merge, >= 0.5 curator, else separate. Unlike the cookbook, we score against labels.

J17.job: Tick off a checklist as a conversation happens
notes: One request per transcript chunk with one Score per unticked item; ticks are one-way; threshold 2.5 on 1-5. Budget is mentioned-but-deferred at chunk 3; compliance is answered with a "no" at chunk 4.

J18.job: Ask more than once, act only when answers agree
notes: 8 runs per ticket with a throwaway uid; odd runs reverse the option order. Code abstains below top probability 0.6. Abstained: 7/64 answers.

J19.job: Ask many questions in one request
notes: Long contract: one request of 10 questions used 1172 tokens vs 7904 for separate requests ($0.000049 vs $0.000332). Separate requests took 3.1 s one after another.
Two questions overlap on purpose (cap_12m and cap_excludes_dp) to check that answers do not leak between questions.

cases.expected: smaller saving than the long document

J20.job: Turn free text into numbers a prediction model can use
notes: 400 synthetic account notes (227 churned); labels drawn at random from planted factors, including a data-quality factor that round 1 does not ask about. AUC = mean (standard error) over 10 x 5-fold cross-validation with logistic regression; "perfect" rows use the true planted factors and mark the ceiling.

cases.expected: question features score higher than word counts
adding the data-quality question raises accuracy
combining narrow questions beats asking for the prediction directly
